- Created the image **`Browser Use`** at `.codx/coworking/images/bu01.browser-use/`:
  - `image.json` — manifest matching `CoworkingImage` in `api/codx/junior/computer/custom_images.py` (id `bu01`, slug `browser-use`, base `lscr.io/linuxserver/webtop:ubuntu-xfce` — already cached locally, live port 3000, user `abc`, tags, status `draft`).
  - `Dockerfile` — venv `/opt/browser-use/.venv` with `browser-use[cli]` + `playwright`, Chromium via `playwright install --with-deps chromium`, venv on `PATH`, menu entry in `/usr/share/applications`.

  - `support/check-browser-use.sh` (versions + which keys the session supplied, never values), `support/browser-use.env.example`, `support/desktop/browser-use.desktop`.

Open the gallery (New coworking session → image library) and check the new **Browser Use** card, or read the folder:

```bash
ls .codx/coworking/images/bu01.browser-use && cd .codx/coworking/images/bu01.browser-use && docker build -t codx-coworking/browser-use:latest .
```

- `quick` — Build `codx-coworking/browser-use:latest`, run it, execute `check-browser-use.sh`, then flip `status` to `ready`.
- `quick` — Make the gallery expose the image ENV list so the session form pre-fills the extra_env fields (needs `env` in `CoworkingImage` + UI).
- `max` — Pin `browser-use` / Playwright versions and add a CI check that rebuilds the image.

"""
Coworking image definitions: the team's own desktop images.

The gallery keeps one folder per image under ``.codx/coworking/images``::

    .codx/coworking/images/<image_id>.<slug>/
        image.json      manifest — the source of truth of this module
        Dockerfile      build recipe (source=dockerfile or dockerhub)
        build.sh        clone + build (source=git)
        README.md       generated summary of the definition
        support/        extra files copied into the image
        media/          icon/screenshot shown in the gallery

Three sources are supported and they all end up as a folder, so the gallery and
the editor treat them the same way:

``dockerfile``
    A base desktop image plus the packages/support files the team needs
    (e.g. Firefox + Jenkins tooling on top of ``lscr.io/linuxserver/webtop``).
``dockerhub``
    An existing Docker Hub image imported by reference; the folder keeps a
    ``FROM <ref>`` recipe so it can still be extended and rebuilt locally.
``git``
    A repository that already contains a Dockerfile; ``build.sh`` clones it and
    builds the image, and the manifest keeps the path/ref of the recipe.

Visibility decides who sees an image in the gallery:

``user``     only its creator;
``project``  every user of the owning project (the default);
``global``   every project of the instance;

# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1
#
# Browser Use — coworking desktop image
#
# Desktop (linuxserver webtop, live view on port 3000) with the browser-use AI
# browser agent ready to drive its own Chromium:
#   https://github.com/browser-use/browser-use
#
# The definition lives in .codx/coworking/images/bu01.browser-use. Credentials
# are never baked into the image: every key below is declared with an empty
# value so the coworking session form (advanced settings -> extra_env) can fill
# it when the session is created.
ARG BASE_IMAGE=lscr.io/linuxserver/webtop:ubuntu-xfce
FROM ${BASE_IMAGE}

# ── Session environment ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Safe defaults are real values; the credential entries are intentionally empty
# and are overwritten by the session (`extra_env`) at runtime.
ENV BROWSER_USE_HOME=/opt/browser-use \
    BROWSER_USE_VENV=/opt/browser-use/.venv \
    BROWSER_USE_HEADLESS=false \
    BROWSER_USE_LOGGING_LEVEL=info \
    BROWSER_USE_CDP_URL=http://127.0.0.1:9222 \
    ANONYMIZED_TELEMETRY=false \
    BROWSER_USE_CLOUD_SYNC=false \
    BROWSER_USE_LLM_MODEL= \
    OPENAI_API_KEY= \
    ANTHROPIC_API_KEY= \
    GOOGLE_API_KEY= \
    DEEPSEEK_API_KEY= \
    OPENROUTER_API_KEY= \
    BROWSER_USE_API_KEY=

# ── System packages ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
USER root
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
RUN apt-get update \
 && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
      build-essential \
      ca-certificates \
      curl \
      git \
      python3 \
      python3-pip \
      python3-venv \
 && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# ── browser-use + its Chromium ────────────────────────────────────────────
# The venv is prepended to PATH further down, so `browser-use` and
# `python -c "import browser_use"` work in every shell of the desktop.
RUN python3 -m venv "${BROWSER_USE_VENV}" \
 && "${BROWSER_USE_VENV}/bin/pip" install --no-cache-dir --upgrade pip wheel \
 && "${BROWSER_USE_VENV}/bin/pip" install --no-cache-dir "browser-use[cli]" playwright

# Chromium plus the system libraries it needs (installed by Playwright itself,
# the same path browser-use recommends upstream).
RUN "${BROWSER_USE_VENV}/bin/python" -m playwright install --with-deps chromium \
 && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

ENV PATH=${BROWSER_USE_VENV}/bin:${PATH}

# ── Support files ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# The menu entry lives in /usr/share/applications so it survives the /config
# volume of the base desktop.
COPY support/check-browser-use.sh /opt/coworking/check-browser-use.sh
COPY support/browser-use.env.example /opt/coworking/browser-use.env.example
COPY support/desktop/browser-use.desktop /usr/share/applications/browser-use.desktop
RUN chmod +x /opt/coworking/check-browser-use.sh \
 && chmod -R a+rX /opt/browser-use /opt/coworking \
 && chown -R abc:abc /opt/browser-use

# ── Metadata ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
ARG IMAGE_VERSION=1.0.0
LABEL org.opencontainers.image.title="Browser Use" \
      org.opencontainers.image.version="${IMAGE_VERSION}" \
      org.opencontainers.image.description="Coworking desktop with the browser-use AI browser agent" \
      org.opencontainers.image.source="codx-junior:coworking/browser-use"

USER abc
EXPOSE 3000

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Smoke test of the browser-use setup of this coworking image.
#
#   /opt/coworking/check-browser-use.sh
#
# Prints the interpreter and browser versions and, without ever showing a
# value, which credentials the session provided through extra_env.
set -uo pipefail

VENV="${BROWSER_USE_VENV:-/opt/browser-use/.venv}"
PY="${VENV}/bin/python"

if [ ! -x "${PY}" ]; then
  echo "browser-use venv not found at ${VENV}" >&2
  exit 1
fi

echo "venv: ${VENV}"
"${PY}" - <<'PYCODE' || exit 1
import sys

import browser_use

version = getattr(browser_use, "__version__", "unknown")
print(f"browser-use {version} (python {sys.version.split()[0]})")
PYCODE

"${PY}" -m playwright --version || exit 1

echo
echo "credentials from the session environment:"
for name in \
  BROWSER_USE_LLM_MODEL \
  OPENAI_API_KEY \
  ANTHROPIC_API_KEY \
  GOOGLE_API_KEY \
  DEEPSEEK_API_KEY \
  OPENROUTER_API_KEY \
  BROWSER_USE_API_KEY; do
  value="${!name:-}"
  if [ -n "${value}" ]; then
    echo "  ${name}: set (${#value} chars)"
  else
    echo "  ${name}: empty"
  fi
done

echo
echo "Empty entries are set when the coworking session is created"
echo "(advanced settings -> extra_env), not inside the image."

request.content:
# Browser Use

Coworking desktop with the **browser-use** AI browser agent
(<https://github.com/browser-use/browser-use>) installed in its own Python venv,
driving the Chromium that Playwright installs inside the image.

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Id | `bu01` |
| Source | `dockerfile` |
| Base image | `lscr.io/linuxserver/webtop:ubuntu-xfce` |
| Live view | port `3000`, desktop user `abc` |
| Docker image | `codx-coworking/browser-use:latest` |
| Status | `draft` until the first build succeeds |

## What the image provides

* `browser-use[cli]` + `playwright` in `/opt/browser-use/.venv`, prepended to
  `PATH`: `browser-use` and `python -c "import browser_use"` work in every
  desktop shell.
* Chromium and its system libraries, installed with
  `python -m playwright install --with-deps chromium`.
* `/opt/coworking/check-browser-use.sh` — versions + which credentials the
  session provided (never prints the values).
* `/opt/coworking/browser-use.env.example` — the same variables the Dockerfile
  declares.
* A **Browser Use** entry in the desktop application menu.

## Session environment (set at session creation)

The Dockerfile declares the credentials with **empty** values on purpose. The
real values are typed by the user when the coworking session is created:

1. New coworking session → image **Browser Use**.
2. Advanced settings → **extra_env**, add the provider key and the model, e.g.

   ```text
   BROWSER_USE_LLM_MODEL=gpt-4o
   OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-...
   ```

3. Start the session and verify inside the desktop:

   ```bash
   /opt/coworking/check-browser-use.sh
   ```

| Variable | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `BROWSER_USE_LLM_MODEL` | Model used by the agent (e.g. `gpt-4o`, `claude-sonnet-4-5`, `gemini-2.5-flash`) |
| `OPENAI_API_KEY` | OpenAI credential |
| `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` | Anthropic credential |
| `GOOGLE_API_KEY` | Google / Gemini credential |
| `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` | DeepSeek credential |
| `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` | OpenRouter credential |
| `BROWSER_USE_API_KEY` | Hosted browser-use API (optional) |
| `BROWSER_USE_HEADLESS` | `false` by default: the agent drives the visible desktop |
| `BROWSER_USE_LOGGING_LEVEL` | `info` by default |
| `BROWSER_USE_CDP_URL` | CDP endpoint the session should reuse (`http://127.0.0.1:9222`) |
| `BROWSER_USE_CLOUD_SYNC`, `ANONYMIZED_TELEMETRY` | Both disabled by default |

Credentials are never written into the image, the manifest or this folder.

## Files

* `image.json` — gallery manifest read by codx-junior.
* `Dockerfile` — build recipe (venv, browser-use, Chromium, env declarations).
* `support/check-browser-use.sh` — in-image smoke test.
* `support/browser-use.env.example` — reference of the session variables.
* `support/desktop/browser-use.desktop` — application-menu entry.

## Build

```bash
cd .codx/coworking/images/bu01.browser-use
docker build -t codx-coworking/browser-use:latest .
```

First build takes a few minutes (pip + Chromium download); the base desktop
`lscr.io/linuxserver/webtop:ubuntu-xfce` is shared with other coworking images.

---

## What happened

1. You asked for a new coworking image for **browser-use**, with **ENV entries** the user fills when creating the session.
2. Review round: **images/media were missing** on the card, the gallery should show **all image types in one catalog** with filters + free text, and an image's **ENV preset** should drive a real **form** (plus mapping an **.env file** to the container).
3. Coworking images in this project are folders in `.codx/coworking/images/<id>.<slug>/` (`image.json` + `Dockerfile` + `support/` + `media/`); sessions receive values through `extra_env`. The **gallery UI and the session form live in the client project**, so the API side is what changed here.

## What I did

**1. Images and media (done)**

- `media/icon.svg` — the card icon (browser window + agent cursor).
- `media/preview.svg` — a 1280×800 preview of the desktop (Chromium + `check-browser-use.sh` + agent panel).
- `image.json` now declares them: `media: ["media/icon.svg", "media/preview.svg"]`, `icon_url`, `screenshot_url`.
- New endpoint so they are actually renderable (`api/codx/junior/api/computer.py`):
  `GET /api/computers/library/custom/{image_id}/media?path=media/icon.svg` → `FileResponse` with the right content type (`_MEDIA_TYPES`: svg/png/jpg/webp/gif). Same visibility check as the other gallery routes (`visible_to`), path sanitised by `library.file_path` → `_safe_relative` (no `..`, no absolute paths).
  *Takes effect after the next API restart — I did not restart the API mid-session.*

**2. ENV preset that can build a form (API part done)**

- New model `ImageEnvField` in `api/codx/junior/computer/custom_images.py`: `name, label, description, placeholder, default, required, secret, choices`.
- `env: List[ImageEnvField]` added to `CoworkingImage`, to `CreateCoworkingImageRequest` and (optional) to `UpdateCoworkingImageRequest`; `create()` stores it. Additive with `default_factory=list`, so **every existing manifest keeps working**.
- `bu01.browser-use/image.json` now ships 8 entries the form can render: `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `GOOGLE_API_KEY`, `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` (all `secret: true`), `BROWSER_USE_LLM_MODEL` (default `gpt-4o-mini`), `BROWSER_USE_HEADLESS` and `BROWSER_USE_LOGGING_LEVEL` (with `choices` → select), `BROWSER_USE_CDP_URL`.
  Verified: the manifest parses into the model and yields 8 `env` fields.

**3. One catalog for every image type (specified, not coded)**

The data already exists in three separate places — curated `list_images(provider, query, category, kind)`, custom coworking images (`/library/custom`) and saved machines (`/library`). The plan is one aggregate route used by a single card grid:

```
GET /api/computers/images/catalog?q=&type=linuxserver,kasmweb,custom,saved&tag=&visibility=&status=&kind=&sort=
→ { facets: { type:{…}, tag:{…}, provider:{…}, visibility:{…} }, items: [ { type, id, name, description, tags, icon_url, preview_url, badges } ] }
```

- One browser, one search box (`q` over name/description/tags), chips for `type`, `tag`, `visibility`, `status` (`draft`/`ready`/`error`) and `kind` (`browser`/`linux`/`windows`/`macos`/`remote`).
- Every card gets `icon_url`/`preview_url` pointing at the same media contract (custom → the new endpoint, saved → `/library/{id}/preview`, catalog → upstream logo), so cards look the same regardless of origin.

**4. Form from the ENV preset + `.env` mapping (specified, not coded)**

- The create-session dialog reads `image.env` and renders one input per entry: `label`, helper text from `description`, `secret` → masked input, `choices` → select, `default` pre-filled, `required` blocking submit. Anything not declared stays available under "extra variables" (`KEY=VALUE`).
- `.env` mapping: a **Map .env file** action on the same screen parses the file, keeps only the keys the image declares (unmatched keys are shown as ignored), and fills the fields instead of sending a blob. Precedence: image `default` < `.env` file < values typed in the form. Names reserved by codx-junior (`SUBFOLDER`, `TITLE`, `DISPLAY`, `VERSION`, `RAM_SIZE`, `CPU_CORES`, `DISK_SIZE`, `USERNAME`, `PASSWORD`) are rejected by the existing rule, and files are not stored — only the resulting `extra_env` enters the session record.
- Secrets are never echoed back: the form shows `set`/`unset`, never the value.

**5. Validation**

- `py_compile` clean on both touched modules; container-side import of `CoworkingImage` over the new manifest → 8 `env` fields, icon/preview paths resolved.
- `qa_review_changes` on the two files: `pytest:api` → **39 passed, 0 failed**; coverage 100 %. Verdict **`require_approval`** for one medium finding: no test added for `custom_images.py`. Nothing is merged until that test exists.

## Demo

Read the card assets and the ENV preset in the manifest:

```bash
ls .codx/coworking/images/bu01.browser-use/media
python3 -m json.tool .codx/coworking/images/bu01.browser-use/image.json | sed -n '/"env"/,/^  ],/p'
```

After the next API restart, `GET /api/computers/library/custom/bu01/media?path=media/icon.svg` returns the icon.

- `max` — Client work: single `/images/catalog` grid with filters + free text, and the ENV-preset form with `.env` mapping on the create-session screen.

Windows/macOS sessions show a dedicated **VM resources** section (vCPUs, RAM
and disk size) in the **New computer session** dialog. Browser/Linux sessions
keep the same resources under *Advanced settings*. The values are stored on the
session record, applied when the machine is created and preserved by restarts
that recreate the container:

| Setting | Browser / Linux | Windows / macOS VM |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Docker image** | Overrides the Chromium/webtop image. A custom image must keep the same live-view and control contract. | Overrides `dockurr/windows` or `dockurr/macos`. |
| **vCPUs** | `docker run --cpus`. | `CPU_CORES` for QEMU (guest CPUs). |
| **RAM** | `docker run --memory`. | `RAM_SIZE` for QEMU (guest RAM). |
| **Disk size** | Not applicable (the container uses the host disk). | `DISK_SIZE`; used when the VM disk is first created. Increasing it and restarting the session expands the existing disk (dockurr keeps the data). |
| **Shared memory** | `docker run --shm-size` (default `2G`). | Not applicable. |
| **Desktop size** | Browser window size / Selkies manual resolution. | Resolution is controlled by the guest OS. |
| **Environment variables** | Extra `-e KEY=VALUE` passed to the image. | Extra `-e KEY=VALUE` passed to the image. |

Environment names managed by codx-junior (`SUBFOLDER`, `TITLE`, `DISPLAY`,
`VERSION`, `RAM_SIZE`, `CPU_CORES`, `DISK_SIZE`, `USERNAME`, `PASSWORD`…) are
reserved: values supplied in the advanced section cannot override them, because
breaking them would detach the live view or the AI control channel.

The same fields are editable after creation from the session's **Session
settings** screen. Use **Save & restart** to apply resource changes: Docker
cannot change CPU/RAM/disk on a running container, so the restart recreates it
while keeping the browser profile and the VM disk. For a macOS VM, 64 GB is the
upstream default; codx-junior defaults macOS to 128 GB, and 256 GB is safer when
installing Xcode/Simulator. On first boot, erase the VirtIO disk in Disk Utility
before reinstalling macOS. After expanding the disk, macOS may need the two
`diskutil` commands documented by
[dockur/macos](https://github.com/dockur/macos) to allocate the extra space.

The API needs the Docker socket (as for workspaces) and, for VMs, the host must
expose `/dev/kvm` (and `/dev/net/tun`). VMs are heavy: at least 2 GB RAM and
32 GB disk per Windows/macOS guest, plus the image pull.

```md docs/features/browser-use.md
# Browser use and co-browsing

> Browser sessions are the `kind="browser"` case of
> [co-desktops](/features/computer-use). The same manager, control lease
> and activity trail now also drive Linux desktops, Windows/macOS VMs and remote
> VNC/SSH machines.

Browser use gives every chat a real Chromium browser that **you and the AI
share**. It is not an AI-only headless browser and not a second "user browser":
there is one page, one history, one cookie jar and one live view.

## What you can do

- Open a browser session from **Coworking** or from a chat and watch the
  page live while the AI works.
- Click, type, scroll and navigate directly in the live view; the AI sees the
  same page on its next tool call.
- Ask the AI to navigate, click, fill forms, run JavaScript, read the page text,
  list links, take screenshots, inspect the HTML source, or review what the user
  did recently.
- Hand control back and forth explicitly. The AI pauses when the human types or
  clicks in the live view, and can request a handoff for login/MFA/captcha.
- Keep the browser profile (cookies, logins, local storage) across restarts.
- Save and replay per-site scripts in one tool call instead of one LLM turn per
  step.
- **Record a flow in the coworking screen** — do "Create a post" once, stop the
  recording, and the generated steps become a recipe the AI can replay. Record
  over an existing recipe to update it (the old version is archived).

## Architecture

```text
                   codx-junior_default Docker network
 ┌────────────────────┐        CDP (port 9223)        ┌──────────────────────┐
 │  API / SmolAgent   │ ────────────────────────────► │  Chromium container  │
 │  Playwright        │                               │  ┌────────────────┐  │
 └─────────┬──────────┘                               │  │ CDP proxy      │  │
           │                                          │  │ 9223 → 9222    │  │
           │ REST / Socket.IO                         │  └────────────────┘  │
 ┌─────────▼──────────┐      Traefik route            │  ┌────────────────┐  │
 │  User browser      │ ────────────────────────────► │  │ Selkies VNC    │  │
 │  live view iframe  │      /browser/<id>/           │  │ port 3000      │  │
 └────────────────────┘                               │  └────────────────┘  │
                                                      └──────────────────────┘
```

- **User control / viewing** — the LinuxServer.io Chromium image exposes a
  Selkies web desktop. Traefik routes it at `/browser/<session_id>/`; the
  session is configured with `SUBFOLDER` so all assets and websockets work
  behind the path prefix.
- **AI control** — Chromium binds DevTools to `127.0.0.1` and rejects non-local
  `Host` headers. A tiny in-container proxy (`cdp_proxy.py`) listens on
  `0.0.0.0:9223`, rewrites the header and tunnels the connection to
  `127.0.0.1:9222`. Playwright connects to the proxy over the shared Docker
  network; both actors therefore drive the **same page**.
- **Persistence** — the container mounts
  `.codx/browser_sessions/<session_id>/chromium_profile` at `/config`.
- **Runtime** — the API keeps one Playwright connection per session (idle
  disconnect after 5 minutes) and serializes actions with a per-session lock.
  A 1-second watcher drains the in-page recorder, so human clicks/edits/tab
  switches show up as `actor=user` activity without polling the whole log.
- **Navigation** — `domcontentloaded` plus a short best-effort `load` wait;
  `networkidle` is no longer used (it timed out on live sites and the old code
  navigated a second time).

## Using it

### From the UI

Open **Coworking**, create a browser session with a name and optional start URL,
then select it. The live browser is embedded in the panel:

- address bar, back, forward and refresh send actions through the REST API;
- clicking and typing in the iframe controls the browser direct

def _desktop_action_params(req: ComputerSessionActionRequest) -> tuple[str, dict]:
    """Convert the API request into backend action parameters."""
    params = req.model_dump(exclude_none=True)
    action = str(params.pop("action", "") or "").lower().strip()
    if "x2" in params and "to_x" not in params:
        params["to_x"] = params["x2"]
    if "y2" in params and "to_y" not in params:
        params["to_y"] = params["y2"]
    # The UI sends the same fields a human would use; drop API-only fields.
    for key in ("session_id", "chat_id", "action"):
        params.pop(key, None)
    return action, params


def _action_message(action: str, result) -> str:
    """Human-readable summary of a desktop action result."""
    if not isinstance(result, dict):
        return f"{action} completed"
    if action == "screenshot":
        text = (result.get("text") or "").strip()
        return (
            f"Screenshot captured ({result.get('width')}x{result.get('height')})"
            + (f"; OCR read {len(text)} chars" if text else "")
        )
    if action == "ocr":
        return f"OCR read {len((result.get('text') or '').strip())} chars"
    if action == "run_command":
        return f"Command exited with {result.get('exit_code')}"
    if action == "windows":
        return f"{len(result.get('windows') or [])} window(s)"
    if action == "click_text":
        matched = result.get("matched") or {}
        return f"Clicked '{matched.get('text')}' at {matched.get('cx')},{matched.get('cy')}"
    if action == "batch":
        return f"Batch finished ({result.get('steps', 0)} step(s))"
    return f"{action} completed"

    Stream one media file of the definition folder.

    if not visible_to(item, username=username, project_id=project_id, is_admin=is_admin):
        raise HTTPException(status_code=403, detail="This image is not shared with you")

@router.post("/{session_id}/action", response_model=BrowserActionResponse, summary="Execute an action")
async def execute_computer_action(
    request: Request,
    session_id: str,
    req: ComputerSessionActionRequest,
):
    """
    Execute an action on the shared machine.

    Browser sessions accept the page actions (navigate, click, fill, snapshot,
    batch...).  Desktop sessions accept the computer actions (screenshot, ocr,
    click, click_text, type, key, run_command, open_app, windows, batch...).

    Desktop coordinates are **display pixels**; the UI scales the rendered
    screenshot back to them before calling this endpoint.
    """
    session_ctx = await get_session_context(request)
    manager = _browser_manager(session_ctx)
    session = manager.get_session(session_id)
    if not session:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Session not found")
    if session.kind == "browser":
        browser_req = BrowserSessionActionRequest(
            action=req.action,
            selector=req.selector,
            ref=req.ref,
            text=req.text,
            value=req.value,
            url=req.url,
            script=req.script,
            key=req.key or req.combo,
            timeout=int(req.timeout * 1000) if req.timeout else 5000,
            x=req.x or 0,
            y=req.y or 0,
            full_page=req.full_page if req.full_page is not None else True,
            steps=req.steps,
            variables=req.variables,
        )
        return await execute_action(request, session_id, browser_req)

    if session.status != "running":
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=400,
            detail=f"Session is not running (status: {session.status})",
        )
    action, params = _desktop_action_params(req)
    if not action:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail="action is required")
    try:
        runtime = await manager.get_runtime(session)
        if action == "batch":
            result = await runtime.run_steps(
                params.get("steps") or [],
                params.get("variables") or {},
                force=True,
                actor="user",
            )
        else:
            result = await runtime.run(action, force=True, actor="user", **params)
        session = getattr(runtime, "session", None) or session
        return BrowserActionResponse(
            success=True,
            message=_action_message(action, result),
            data=result if isinstance(result, dict) else {"result": result},
        )
    except ComputerControlError as ex:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=409, detail=str(ex))
    except UnsupportedComputerActionError as ex:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail=str(ex))
    except DesktopControlError as ex:
        logger.warning("Desktop action '%s' failed for %s: %s", action, session_id[:8], ex)
        raise HTTPException(status_code=502, detail=str(ex))
    except HTTPException:
        raise
    except Exception as ex:
        logger.exception("Desktop action '%s' failed: %s", action, ex)
        raise HTTPException(status_code=500, detail=str(ex))


@router.post("/{session_id}/screenshot", response_model=BrowserScreenshotResponse, summary="Screenshot")
async def take_computer_screenshot(
    request: Request,
    session_id: str,
    req: Optional[ComputerScreenshotRequest] = None,
):
    """Capture the page (browser) or desktop (computer) as a PNG data URI."""
    session_ctx = await get_session_context(request)
    manager = _browser_manager(session_ctx)
    session = manager.get_session(session_id)
    if not session:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Session not found")
    if session.kind == "browser":
        return await take_browser_screenshot(request, session_id, req)
    if session.status != "running":
        return BrowserScreenshotResponse(success=False, error="Session is not running")
    try:
        runtime = await manager.get_runtime(session)
        result = await runtime.screenshot(
            include_text=bool(req.include_text) if req and req.include_text is not None else True,
            max_width=int(req.max_width) if req and req.max_width else 1600,
            actor="user",
        )
        return BrowserScreenshotResponse(
            success=True,
            screenshot=result.get("image"),
            data={key: value for key, value in result.items() if key != "image"},
        )
    except Exception as ex:
        logger.warning("Computer screenshot failed for %s: %s", session_id[:8], ex)
        return BrowserScreenshotResponse(success=False, error=str(ex))

async def create_vnc_ticket(request: Request, session_id: str):
    """
    Return a short-lived WebSocket path for the built-in noVNC viewer.

    The path is relative and already contains the ticket, so the long-lived JWT
    is never placed in a WebSocket URL.  The ticket is bound to this session's
    VNC endpoint and can be redeemed once.

    manager = _browser_manager(session_ctx)
    session = manager.get_session(session_id)

                "their web live view (vnc_url/vnc_path)"

    user = getattr(getattr(session_ctx, "user", None), "username", "") or ""
    ticket = vnc_tickets.issue(

        port=session.vnc_port or 5900,
        user=user,
        session=session,
        manager=manager,
    )
    return ComputerVncTicketResponse(
        session_id=session.id,
        socket_path=f"/api/computers/{session.id}/vnc?ticket={ticket.value}",
        # The ticket is already authenticated and single-use; giving the viewer
        # the session password here avoids putting it in the general session
        # record that the UI/Socket.IO receive.
        password=session.vnc_password,
        expires_in=vnc_tickets.ttl,

@router.websocket("/{session_id}/vnc")
async def computer_vnc_websocket(
    websocket: WebSocket,
    session_id: str,
    ticket: str = Query("", description="Single-use ticket from POST …/vnc-ticket"),
):
    """Tunnel raw RFB bytes between the browser's noVNC client and the machine."""
    ticket_data = vnc_tickets.consume(ticket)
    if ticket_data is None:
        # Close before accept: no unauthenticated WebSocket is upgraded.
        await websocket.close(code=4401, reason="Invalid or expired VNC ticket")
        return
    if ticket_data.session_id != session_id:
        await websocket.close(code=4403, reason="Ticket does not match this session")
        return
    await websocket.accept()
    logger.info(
        "VNC bridge open: session=%s host=%s:%s user=%s",
        session_id[:8], ticket_data.host, ticket_data.port, ticket_data.user or "-",
    )

    last_input = {"at": 0.0}

    def on_user_input():
        """Mark the human active (throttled) when their RFB input crosses."""
        now = time.monotonic()
        if now - last_input["at"] < 1.0:
            return
        last_input["at"] = now
        target = ticket_data.session
        if target is None:
            return
        target.mark_user_active(seconds=10)
        manager = ticket_data.manager
        if manager is not None:
            try:
                manager.save_session(target)
                from codx.junior.browser import events as browser_events
                browser_events.broadcast_control(target)
            except Exception:
                logger.debug("Could not persist VNC user activity", exc_info=True)

    await bridge_vnc(
        websocket,
        ticket_data.host,
        ticket_data.port,
        on_input=on_user_input,
    )
    logger.info("VNC bridge closed: session=%s", session_id[:8])

"""
Coworking image definitions: the team's own desktop images.

The gallery keeps one folder per image under ``.codx/coworking/images``::

    .codx/coworking/images/<image_id>.<slug>/
        image.json      manifest — the source of truth of this module
        Dockerfile      build recipe (source=dockerfile or dockerhub)
        build.sh        clone + build (source=git)
        README.md       generated summary of the definition
        support/        extra files copied into the image
        media/          icon/screenshot shown in the gallery

Three sources are supported and they all end up as a folder, so the gallery and
the editor treat them the same way:

``dockerfile``
    A base desktop image plus the packages/support files the team needs
    (e.g. Firefox + Jenkins tooling on top of ``lscr.io/linuxserver/webtop``).
``dockerhub``
    An existing Docker Hub image imported by reference; the folder keeps a
    ``FROM <ref>`` recipe so it can still be extended and rebuilt locally.
``git``
    A repository that already contains a Dockerfile; ``build.sh`` clones it and
    builds the image, and the manifest keeps the path/ref of the recipe.

Visibility decides who sees an image in the gallery:

``user``     only its creator;
``project``  every user of the owning project (the default);
``global``   every project of the instance;
``custom``   only the projects listed in ``projects``.

The heavy lifting of writing a real Dockerfile (packages, entrypoints, testing
the build) is delegated to the ``codx-junior-max`` assistant: :func:`build_prompt`
renders the instruction the UI sends to that chat, pointing at the folder.

def _safe_relative(relative_path: str) -> str:
    """Normalise a folder-relative path and refuse anything that escapes it."""
    cleaned = (relative_path or "").replace("\\", "/").strip().lstrip("/")

    if not parts:
        raise ValueError("A file path inside the image folder is required")
    if any(part == ".." for part in parts):
        raise ValueError(f"Invalid file path: {relative_path}")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Templates
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def _dockerfile_template(
    name: str,
    description: str,
    base_image: str,
    desktop_user: str,
    live_port: int,
    slug: str,
) -> str:
    return f"""# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1
#
# {name} — coworking desktop image
#
# {description or "Custom desktop image for codx-junior coworking."}
#
# The folder .codx/coworking/images holds the definition; the codx-junior-max
# assistant fills the packages and support files below and validates the build.
ARG BASE_IMAGE={base_image}
FROM ${{BASE_IMAGE}}

# ── System packages ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Install what the image must provide, e.g. a browser and the CI/CD tooling:
#   firefox-esr  chromium  openjdk-17-jre  nodejs  npm  git  curl
USER root
RUN apt-get update \\
 && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \\
      firefox-esr \\
      git \\
      curl \\
 && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# ── Support files ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Files of this folder are copied from support/ (desktop entries, configs...).
# COPY support/ /opt/coworking/
# COPY support/desktop/ /config/Desktop/

# ── Metadata ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
ARG IMAGE_VERSION=1.0.0
LABEL org.opencontainers.image.title="{name}" \\
      org.opencontainers.image.version="${{IMAGE_VERSION}}" \\
      org.opencontainers.image.description="{description or name}" \\
      org.opencontainers.image.source="codx-junior:coworking/{slug}"

USER {desktop_user}
EXPOSE {live_port}
"""


def _dockerhub_dockerfile(reference: str, name: str, slug: str) -> str:
    return f"""# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1
#
# {name} — imported from Docker Hub
#
# The upstream image is used as-is; keep the FROM and add the extra layers
# this team needs (they will be part of every coworking session).
ARG BASE_IMAGE={reference}
FROM ${{BASE_IMAGE}}

# Add the team layers here, for example:
# USER root
# RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends <packages> \\
#  && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

LABEL org.opencontainers.image.source="codx-junior:coworking/{slug}"
"""


def _git_build_script(git_url: str, git_ref: str, image: str) -> str:
    ref = git_ref or "main"
    return f"""#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Build the coworking image from its repository.
#
# The repository is the source of truth of the recipe; this script clones the
# requested ref and runs the docker build the repository ships.
set -euo pipefail

REPO="{git_url}"
IMAGE="{image}"

workdir="$(mktemp -d)"
trap 'rm -rf "$workdir"' EXIT

git clone --depth 1 --branch "{ref}" "$REPO" "$workdir/repo"
docker build -t "$IMAGE" "$workdir/repo"
echo "Built $IMAGE from $REPO@{ref}"
"""


def _readme_template(item: CoworkingImage) -> str:
    lines = [
        f"# {item.name}",
        "",
        item.description or "Custom desktop image of the coworking gallery.",
        "",
        "| Field | Value |",
        "| --- | --- |",
        f"| Id | `{item.id}` |",
        f"| Source | `{item.source}` |",
        f"| Visibility | `{item.visibility}`"
        + (f" ({', '.join(item.projects)})" if item.projects else ""),
        "| Base image | `{}` |".format(item.base_image or "-"),
        "| Docker Hub | `{}` |".format(item.docker_ref or "-"),
        "| Repository | `{}` |".format(item.git_url or "-"),
        "| Tags | {} |".format(", ".join(f"`{tag}`" for tag in item.tags) or "-"),
        f"| Owner | `{item.created_by or '-'}` |",
        f"| Status | `{item.status}` |",
        "",
        "## Files",
        "",
        f"* `{MANIFEST_FILE}` — this definition, read by codx-junior.",
        f"* `{item.dockerfile}` — build recipe of the image.",
    ]
    if item.build_script:
        lines.append(f"* `{item.build_script}` — clone + build helper of the repository.")
    lines += [
        f"* `{SUPPORT_FOLDER}/` — files copied into the image.",
        f"* `{MEDIA_FOLDER}/` — icon and preview shown in the gallery.",
        "",
        "## Build",
        "",
        "```bash",
        f"docker build -t {item.docker_image()} .",
        "```",
        "",
        "Hand the folder to the `codx-junior-max` assistant to complete the recipe:",
        "",
        "```text",
        item.assistant_prompt,
        "```",
        "",
    ]
    return "\n".join(lines)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Visibility
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def visible_to(
    item: CoworkingImage,
    username: Optional[str] = None,
    project_id: Optional[str] = None,
    is_admin: bool = False,
) -> bool:
    """Whether a user of ``project_id`` may see this image in the gallery."""
    if is_admin:
        return True
    visibility = (item.visibility or "project").lower()
    if visibility == "global":
        return True
    if visibility == "user":
        return bool(username) and item.created_by == username
    if visibility == "custom":
        return bool(project_id) and project_id in (item.projects or [])
    return bool(project_id) and item.project_id == project_id


def can_edit(
    item: CoworkingImage,
    username: Optional[str] = None,
    project_id: Optional[str] = None,
    is_admin: bool = False,
) -> bool:
    """Owner, project admin role and global entries: see the API router."""
    if is_admin:
        return True
    if item.created_by and item.created_by == username:
        return True
    if (item.visibility or "project").lower() == "user":
        return False
    return bool(project_id) and item.project_id == project_id


def build_prompt(item: CoworkingImage, folder_path: str) -> str:
    """Instruction that hands the folder to the ``codx-junior-max`` assistant."""
    origin = {
        "dockerfile": f"base image `{item.base_image or DEFAULT_BASE_IMAGE}`",
        "dockerhub": f"Docker Hub reference `{item.docker_ref}`",
        "git": f"repository `{item.git_url}` (ref `{item.git_ref or 'main'}`)",
    }.get(item.source, f"source `{item.source}`")
    return (
        f"As the `{ASSISTANT_PROFILE}` assistant, create the coworking desktop image "
        f"**{item.name}** in the folder "
        f"`{os.path.join(folder_path, MANIFEST_FILE)}` (definition) and "
        f"`{os.path.join(folder_path, item.dockerfile)}` (recipe).\n\n"
        f"* Source: {origin}.\n"
        f"* Purpose: {item.description or 'custom desktop image for the team'}.\n"
        f"* Tags: {', '.join(item.tags) or 'none'}.\n"
        f"* Live view: port {item.live_port or DEFAULT_LIVE_PORT}, desktop user "
        f"`{item.desktop_user}`.\n\n"
        "Steps:\n"
        "1. Complete the Dockerfile (packages, support files, entrypoint) keeping "
        "the live-view service of the base desktop working.\n"
        "2. Add the support files under `support/` and the gallery icon/preview "
        f"under `{MEDIA_FOLDER}/`; list them in `{MANIFEST_FILE}` "
        "(media, support_files, icon_url, screenshot_url).\n"
        "3. Build the image and smoke-test that the desktop starts.\n"
        f"4. Set `status` to `ready` (or `error` with the message) in `{MANIFEST_FILE}`.\n"
    )


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Library
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
class CoworkingImageLibrary:
    """Filesystem-backed gallery of custom coworking images."""

    def __init__(self, codx_path: str, project_id: Optional[str] = None, project_name: Optional[str] = None):
        self.codx_path = codx_path
        self.project_id = project_id
        self.project_name = project_name
        self.root = os.path.join(codx_path, COWORKING_FOLDER, IMAGES_FOLDER)
        os.makedirs(self.root, exist_ok=True)

    # ── paths ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    def folder_name(self, item: CoworkingImage) -> str:
        """``<image_id>.<slug>``: a stable, human-readable folder name."""
        return f"{item.id}.{item.slug}"

    def folder_path(self, image_id: str) -> Optional[str]:
        if not image_id:
            return None
        for folder in Path(self.root).iterdir():
            if not folder.is_dir() or folder.name == ".trash":
                continue
            if folder.name == image_id or folder.name.split(".")[0] == image_id:
                if os.path.isfile(str(folder / MANIFEST_FILE)):
                    return str(folder)
        return None

    def file_path(self, image_id: str, relative_path: str) -> str:
        folder = self.folder_path(image_id)
        if not folder:
            raise FileNotFoundError(image_id)
        return os.path.join(folder, _safe_relative(relative_path))

    # ── CRUD ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    def list(self) -> List[CoworkingImage]:
        items: List[CoworkingImage] = []
        if not os.path.isdir(self.root):
            return items
        for folder in Path(self.root).iterdir():
            if not folder.is_dir() or folder.name == ".trash":
                continue
            item = self._read(str(folder / MANIFEST_FILE))
            if item:
                items.append(item)
        items.sort(key=lambda entry: entry.updated_at or entry.created_at or "", reverse=True)
        return items

    def list_visible(
        self,
        username: Optional[str] = None,
        project_id: Optional[str] = None,
        is_admin: bool = False,
        q: Optional[str] = None,
        visibility: Optional[str] = None,
        tag: Optional[str] = None,
    ) -> List[CoworkingImage]:
        needle = (q or "").strip().lower()
        wanted_tag = (tag or "").strip().lower()
        wanted_visibility = (visibility or "").strip().lower()
        result = []
        for item in self.list():
            if not visible_to(item, username=username, project_id=project_id, is_admin=is_admin):
                continue
            if wanted_visibility and item.visibility != wanted_visibility:
                continue
            if wanted_tag and wanted_tag not in [entry.lower() for entry in item.tags]:
                continue
            if needle:
                haystack = " ".join(
                    [item.name, item.description, item.slug, " ".join(item.tags), item.docker_ref or "", item.git_url or ""]
                ).lower()
                if needle not in haystack:
                    continue
            result.append(item)
        return result

    def get(self, image_id: str) -> Optional[CoworkingImage]:
        if not image_id:
            return None
        folder = self.folder_path(image_id)
        return self._read(os.path.join(folder, MANIFEST_FILE)) if folder else None

    def save(self, item: CoworkingImage) -> CoworkingImage:
        folder = os.path.join(self.root, self.folder_name(item))
        os.makedirs(folder, exist_ok=True)
        for name in (SUPPORT_FOLDER, MEDIA_FOLDER):
            os.makedirs(os.path.join(folder, name), exist_ok=True)
        item.folder = os.path.basename(folder)
        item.updated_at = _now()
        stored = item.model_copy(update={"assistant_prompt": ""})
        tmp = os.path.join(folder, MANIFEST_FILE + ".tmp")
        with open(tmp, "w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
            json.dump(stored.to_dict(), handle, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False)
        os.replace(tmp, os.path.join(folder, MANIFEST_FILE))
        try:
            os.chmod(os.path.join(folder, MANIFEST_FILE), MANIFEST_MODE)
        except OSError:
            pass
        item.assistant_prompt = build_prompt(item, folder)
        return item

    def delete(self, image_id: str) -> bool:
        folder = self.folder_path(image_id)
        if not folder:
            return False
        shutil.rmtree(folder, ignore_errors=True)
        return True

    # ── creation / import ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
    def create(
        self,
        req: CreateCoworkingImageRequest,
        created_by: Optional[str] = None,
    ) -> CoworkingImage:
        name = (req.name or "").strip()
        if not name:
            raise ValueError("The image needs a name")
        source = (req.source or "dockerfile").strip().lower()
        if source not in SOURCES:
            raise ValueError(f"Unknown source '{req.source}'. Use one of: {', '.join(SOURCES)}")
        visibility = (req.visibility or "project").strip().lower()
        if visibility not in VISIBILITIES:
            raise ValueError(f"Unknown visibility '{req.visibility}'. Use one of: {', '.join(VISIBILITIES)}")
        projects = [entry.strip() for entry in (req.projects or []) if entry and entry.strip()]
        if visibility == "custom" and not projects:
            raise ValueError("visibility=custom needs at least one project")
        if source == "dockerhub" and not (req.docker_ref or "").strip():
            raise ValueError("A Docker Hub import needs the image reference")
        if source == "git" and not (req.git_url or "").strip():
            raise ValueError("A repository import needs the git URL")

        slug = _slug(name)
        item = CoworkingImage(
            id=uuid.uuid4().hex[:8],
            slug=slug,
            name=name,
            description=(req.description or "").strip(),
            source=source,
            base_image=(req.base_image or "").strip() or (
                (req.docker_ref or "").strip() if source == "dockerhub" else DEFAULT_BASE_IMAGE
            ),
            docker_ref=(req.docker_ref or "").strip() or None,
            git_url=(req.git_url or "").strip() or None,
            git_ref=(req.git_ref or "").strip() or None,
            media=[entry for entry in (req.media or []) if entry],
            icon_url=req.icon_url or None,
            screenshot_url=req.screenshot_url or None,
            env=[
                entry
                for entry in (req.env or [])
                if (entry.name or "").strip()
            ],
            tags=[entry for entry in (req.tags or []) if entry],
            visibility=visibility,
            projects=projects,
            created_by=created_by,
            project_id=self.project_id,
            project_name=self.project_name,
            created_at=_now(),
            updated_at=_now(),
            status="draft",
            live_port=req.live_port or DEFAULT_LIVE_PORT,
        )
        self.save(item)
        if req.scaffold:
            self._scaffold(item)
        return self.get(item.id) or item

    def _scaffold(self, item: CoworkingImage) -> None:
        """Write the starter files; safe to call twice (never overwrites)."""
        folder = self.folder_path(item.id)
        if not folder:
            return
        dockerfile = os.path.join(folder, getattr(item, "dockerfile", DOCKERFILE_FILE))
        if not os.path.exists(dockerfile):
            if item.source == "dockerhub":
                content = _dockerhub_dockerfile(item.docker_ref or item.base_image or "", item.name, item.slug)
            else:
                content = _dockerfile_template(
                    item.name,
                    item.description,
                    item.base_image or DEFAULT_BASE_IMAGE,
                    item.desktop_user,
                    item.live_port or DEFAULT_LIVE_PORT,
                    item.slug,
                )
            _write_file(dockerfile, content)
        if item.source == "git" and item.git_url:
            script = os.path.join(folder, BUILD_SCRIPT)
            if not os.path.exists(script):
                _write_file(
                    script,
                    _git_build_script(item.git_url, item.git_ref or "main", item.docker_image()),
                    executable=True,
                )
            item.build_script = BUILD_SCRIPT
        item.support_files = sorted(
            {
                entry.path
                for entry in self.files(item.id)
                if not entry.is_manifest and entry.path != README_FILE
            }
        )
        self.save(item)
        _write_file(os.path.join(folder, README_FILE), _readme_template(item))

    def import_from_dockerhub(self, reference: str, created_by: Optional[str] = None, **kwargs: Any) -> CoworkingImage:
        """Import an existing Docker Hub image as a coworking image."""
        reference = (reference or "").strip()
        if not reference:
            raise ValueError("A Docker Hub reference is required")
        name = kwargs.pop("name", None) or reference.split(":")[0].split("/")[-1]
        req = CreateCoworkingImageRequest(
            name=name,
            source="dockerhub",
            docker_ref=reference,
            description=kwargs.pop("description", None) or f"Imported from Docker Hub: {reference}",
            tags=kwargs.pop("tags", []) or ["imported", "dockerhub"],
            **kwargs,
        )
        return self.create(req, created_by=created_by)

    def import_from_git(self, git_url: str, created_by: Optional[str] = None, **kwargs: Any) -> CoworkingImage:
        """Import a repository that already ships a Dockerfile."""
        git_url = (git_url or "").strip()
        if not git_url:
            raise ValueError("A repository URL is required")
        name = kwargs.pop("name", None) or git_url.rstrip("/").split("/")[-1].removesuffix(".git")
        req = CreateCoworkingImageRequest(
            name=name,
            source="git",
            git_url=git_url,
            git_ref=kwargs.pop("git_ref", None) or "main",
            description=kwargs.pop("description", None) or f"Imported from repository: {git_url}",
            tags=kwargs.pop("tags", []) or ["imported", "git"],
            **kwargs,
        )
        return self.create(req, created_by=created_by)

    def update(self, image_id: str, req: UpdateCoworkingImageRequest) -> Optional[CoworkingImage]:
        item = self.get(image_id)
        if not item:
            return None
        changes = req.model_dump(exclude_none=True)
        if "visibility" in changes:
            visibility = str(changes["visibility"]).strip().lower()
            if visibility not in VISIBILITIES:
                raise ValueError(f"Unknown visibility '{visibility}'. Use one of: {', '.join(VISIBILITIES)}")
            changes["visibility"] = visibility
        if "source" in changes:
            source = str(changes["source"]).strip().lower()
            if source not in SOURCES:
                raise ValueError(f"Unknown source '{source}'. Use one of: {', '.join(SOURCES)}")
            changes["source"] = source
        if "name" in changes and changes["name"]:
            item.slug = _slug(str(changes["name"]), item.slug)
        updated = item.model_copy(update=changes)
        if updated.visibility == "custom" and not updated.projects:
            raise ValueError("visibility=custom needs at least one project")
        return self.save(updated)

    # ── files ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    def files(self, image_id: str) -> List[ImageFileInfo]:
        folder = self.folder_path(image_id)
        if not folder:
            return []
        result: List[ImageFileInfo] = []
        for path in sorted(Path(folder).rglob("*")):
            if not path.is_file() or path.name.endswith(".tmp"):
                continue
            relative = str(path.relative_to(folder)).replace(os.sep, "/")
            result.append(
                ImageFileInfo(
                    path=relative,
                    size=path.stat().st_size,
                    is_manifest=relative == MANIFEST_FILE,
                )
            )
        return result

    def read_file(self, image_id: str, relative_path: str) -> ImageFileContent:
        path = self.file_path(image_id, relative_path)
        if not os.path.isfile(path):
            raise FileNotFoundError(relative_path)
        with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as handle:
            return ImageFileContent(path=_safe_relative(relative_path), content=handle.read())

    def write_file(self, image_id: str, relative_path: str, content: str) -> ImageFileContent:
        path = self.file_path(image_id, relative_path)
        _write_file(path, content, executable=path.endswith(".sh"))
        item = self.get(image_id)
        if item:
            item.support_files = sorted(
                {entry.path for entry in self.files(image_id) if not entry.is_manifest and entry.path != README_FILE}
            )
            self.save(item)
        return ImageFileContent(path=_safe_relative(relative_path), content=content)

    def prompt_for(self, image_id: str) -> Optional[str]:
        item = self.get(image_id)
        folder = self.folder_path(image_id)
        if not item or not folder:
            return None
        return build_prompt(item, folder)

    # ── internals ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    @staticmethod
    def _read(path: str) -> Optional[CoworkingImage]:
        try:
            with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
                item = CoworkingImage(**json.load(handle))
        except FileNotFoundError:
            return None
        except Exception as ex:  # pragma: no cover - corrupt manifest
            logger.warning("Could not read coworking image '%s': %s", path, ex)
            return None
        item.folder = os.path.basename(os.path.dirname(path))
        item.assistant_prompt = build_prompt(item, os.path.dirname(path))
        return item


def _write_file(path: str, content: str, executable: bool = False) -> None:
    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(path), exist_ok=True)
    with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
        handle.write(content)
    if executable:
        try:
            os.chmod(path, 0o755)
        except OSError:
            pass


def coworking_image_library(settings: Any) -> CoworkingImageLibrary:
    """Return the gallery of the project behind ``settings``."""
    return CoworkingImageLibrary(
        codx_path=settings.codx_path,
        project_id=getattr(settings, "project_id", None),
        project_name=getattr(settings, "project_name", None),
    )

```js
/**
 * ENV preset of a coworking image.
 * ...
 */

const NAME_PATTERN = /^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$/

/**
 * ENV entries declared by an image manifest (`env` in `image.json`).
 *
 * Accepts both the gallery card (`{ coworking_image: { env } }`) and a plain
 * manifest, and drops entries without a usable name so a malformed manifest
 * never renders an empty row.
 */
export function declaredEnv(image) {
  const fields = image?.coworking_image?.env ?? image?.env ?? []
  if (!Array.isArray(fields)) return []
  return fields.filter(field => field && typeof field.name === 'string' && NAME_PATTERN.test(field.name))
}

/**
 * Parse `.env` text into a plain object.
 *
 * Supports `export KEY=value`, `#` comments, blank lines, quoted values
 * (`"a b"`, `'a b'`) and values containing `=`. A line without `=` or with an
 * invalid name is skipped (an `.env` file is user input, not a form field).
 */
export function parseDotEnv(text) {
  const values = {}
  String(text ?? '').split('\n').forEach(raw => {
    const line = raw.trim().replace(/^export\s+/, '')
    if (!line || line.startsWith('#')) return
    const separator = line.indexOf('=')
    if (separator <= 0) return
    const name = line.slice(0, separator).trim()
    if (!NAME_PATTERN.test(name)) return
    values[name] = unquote(line.slice(separator + 1).trim())
  })
  return values
}

/** Strip one pair of matching surrounding quotes. */
export function unquote(value) {
  const text = String(value ?? '').trim()
  if (text.length < 2) return text
  const first = text[0]
  const last = text[text.length - 1]
  if ((first === '"' || first === "'") && first === last) return text.slice(1, -1)
  return text
}

/** Values of an untouched form: the defaults declared by the manifest. */
export function presetDefaults(fields) {
  const values = {}
  fields.forEach(field => { values[field.name] = field.default ?? '' })
  return values
}

/**
 * Map an `.env` object onto the declared fields.
 * ...
 * @returns {{values: Object, mapped: string[], ignored: string[]}}
 */
export function mapDotEnv(fields, dotEnv) {
  const declared = new Set(fields.map(f => f.name))
  const values = {}
  const ignored = []
  Object.entries(dotEnv || {}).forEach(([name, value]) => {
    if (!declared.has(name)) {
      ignored.push(name)
      return
    }
    values[name] = value
  })
  return { values, mapped: Object.keys(values), ignored }
}

/** Non-empty (trimmed) values of the form: what travels as `extra_env`. */
export function presetValues(fields, typed) {
  const values = {}
  fields.forEach(field => {
    const value = String(typed?.[field.name] ?? '').trim()
    if (value) values[field.name] = value
  })
  return values
}

/** Required fields left empty; returns their labels (or names). */
export function missingRequired(fields, values) {
  return fields
    .filter(field => field.required && !String(values?.[field.name] ?? '').trim())
    .map(field => field.label || field.name)
}

  ...
}

# .codx/coworking/images/bu01.browser-use/Dockerfile (lines 1-80 of 80)
``` .codx/coworking/images/bu01.browser-use/Dockerfile
# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1
#
# Browser Use — coworking desktop image
#
# Desktop (linuxserver webtop, live view on port 3000) with the browser-use AI
# browser agent ready to drive its own Chromium:
#   https://github.com/browser-use/browser-use
#
# The definition lives in .codx/coworking/images/bu01.browser-use. Credentials
# are never baked into the image: every key below is declared with an empty
# value so the coworking session form (advanced settings -> extra_env) can fill
# it when the session is created.
ARG BASE_IMAGE=lscr.io/linuxserver/webtop:ubuntu-xfce
FROM ${BASE_IMAGE}

# ── Session environment ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Safe defaults are real values; the credential entries are intentionally empty
# and are overwritten by the session (`extra_env`) at runtime.
ENV BROWSER_USE_HOME=/opt/browser-use \
    BROWSER_USE_VENV=/opt/browser-use/.venv \
    BROWSER_USE_HEADLESS=false \
    BROWSER_USE_LOGGING_LEVEL=info \
    BROWSER_USE_CDP_URL=http://127.0.0.1:9222 \
    ANONYMIZED_TELEMETRY=false \
    BROWSER_USE_CLOUD_SYNC=false \
    BROWSER_USE_LLM_MODEL= \
    OPENAI_API_KEY= \
    ANTHROPIC_API_KEY= \
    GOOGLE_API_KEY= \
    DEEPSEEK_API_KEY= \
    OPENROUTER_API_KEY= \
    BROWSER_USE_API_KEY=

# ── System packages ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
USER root
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
RUN apt-get update \
 && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
      build-essential \
      ca-certificates \
      curl \
      git \
      python3 \
      python3-pip \
      python3-venv \
 && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# ── browser-use + its Chromium ────────────────────────────────────────────
# The venv is prepended to PATH further down, so `browser-use` and
# `python -c "import browser_use"` work in every shell of the desktop.
RUN python3 -m venv "${BROWSER_USE_VENV}" \
 && "${BROWSER_USE_VENV}/bin/pip" install --no-cache-dir --upgrade pip wheel \
 && "${BROWSER_USE_VENV}/bin/pip" install --no-cache-dir "browser-use[cli]" playwright

# Chromium plus the system libraries it needs (installed by Playwright itself,
# the same path browser-use recommends upstream).
RUN "${BROWSER_USE_VENV}/bin/python" -m playwright install --with-deps chromium \
 && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

ENV PATH=${BROWSER_USE_VENV}/bin:${PATH}

# ── Support files ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# The menu entry lives in /usr/share/applications so it survives the /config
# volume of the base desktop.
COPY support/check-browser-use.sh /opt/coworking/check-browser-use.sh
COPY support/browser-use.env.example /opt/coworking/browser-use.env.example
COPY support/desktop/browser-use.desktop /usr/share/applications/browser-use.desktop
RUN chmod +x /opt/coworking/check-browser-use.sh \
 && chmod -R a+rX /opt/browser-use /opt/coworking \
 && chown -R abc:abc /opt/browser-use

# ── Metadata ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
ARG IMAGE_VERSION=1.0.0
LABEL org.opencontainers.image.title="Browser Use" \
      org.opencontainers.image.version="${IMAGE_VERSION}" \
      org.opencontainers.image.description="Coworking desktop with the browser-use AI browser agent" \
      org.opencontainers.image.source="codx-junior:coworking/browser-use"

USER abc
EXPOSE 3000
```

request.content:
# Build helper for this coworking image.
#
# `docker build` of this folder takes several minutes (apt + browser-use +
# Playwright Chromium), longer than a single assistant tool call is allowed to
# block. Running it through compose keeps the builder attached to the daemon
# while the rest of the work continues:
#
#   docker compose -f .codx/coworking/images/bu01.browser-use/build.compose.yaml up -d
#   docker compose -f .codx/coworking/images/bu01.browser-use/build.compose.yaml logs -f
#
# It uses the image of the project itself (`codx:current` when it exists, else
# any image with a docker CLI) and the host daemon through the socket.
services:
  builder:
    image: ${COWORKING_BUILDER_IMAGE:-docker:cli}
    working_dir: /src
    volumes:
      - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock
      - .:/src:ro
    command:
      ["build", "--progress=plain", "-t", "codx-coworking/browser-use:latest", "."]

    if [ ! -f dist/index.html ]; then
      echo "ERROR: client/dist is missing; build it once with: npm run build-only" >&2
      exit 1
    fi
    npm run preview
    ;;
esac

#!/bin/bash
# Dynamically set CODX_JUNIOR_PATH to the parent directory of the script
export CODX_JUNIOR_PATH="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
echo "CODX_JUNIOR_PATH: $CODX_JUNIOR_PATH"
echo "Starting api USER: ${USER} ($(id -u):$(id -g)) HOME: ${HOME}"

# A packaged image (see codx-junior-installer/demo) already ships the venv and a
# source tree it must not touch: the recursive chown and `uv sync` below are
# installation steps, not start-up steps, and cost tens of seconds per restart.
# Set CODX_JUNIOR_SKIP_INSTALL=1 to skip them.
if [ "$CODX_JUNIOR_SKIP_INSTALL" != "1" ]; then
  echo "Fix permissions"
  sudo chown -R ${USER} ${HOME} & 
  sudo chown ${USER} /var/run/docker.sock 2>/dev/null || true
fi

source ${CODX_JUNIOR_PATH}/set_env.sh

export PYTHONPATH=${CODX_JUNIOR_PATH}/api

cd ${CODX_JUNIOR_PATH}/api


# Run the FastAPI application using uvicorn
echo "Checking venv: '${CODX_JUNIOR_API_VENV}' ..."
if [ ! -d "${CODX_JUNIOR_API_VENV}/bin" ]; then
  echo "!!! venv not found. Installing at: ${CODX_JUNIOR_API_VENV}"
  bash ${CODX_JUNIOR_PATH}/scripts/install_api.sh
else
  echo "venv found!"
fi

source ${CODX_JUNIOR_API_VENV}/bin/activate

if [ "$CODX_JUNIOR_SKIP_INSTALL" != "1" ]; then
  # Sync the environment with pyproject.toml / uv.lock on start (development and
  # source-mounted deployments only: it downloads packages).
  uv sync
fi

echo "codx-junior api BACKGROUND: '${CODX_JUNIOR_API_BACKGROUND}' DEBUG: '${DEBUG}'"

API_PORT=$CODX_JUNIOR_API_PORT
if [ "$CODX_JUNIOR_API_BACKGROUND" != "" ]; then
  API_PORT=$CODX_JUNIOR_API_PORT_BACKGROUND
fi

if [ "$DEBUG" == "" ]; then
  echo "Running PROD api"
  # ONE worker by default: Socket.IO keeps the connected sessions (and the
  # in-memory CancellationTokens of the running turns) inside the process, so
  # with several workers a client reconnects/re-emits against another worker and
  # its chat looks stuck. Scale explicitly with WEB_CONCURRENCY only when a
  # shared Socket.IO message queue is configured.
  uvicorn codx.junior.main:app --workers ${WEB_CONCURRENCY:-1} --host 0.0.0.0 --port $API_PORT
elif [ "$CODX_JUNIOR_API_RELOAD" == "1" ] || [ "$CODX_JUNIOR_API_RELOAD" == "true" ]; then
  # Opt-in source reload for development ONLY. Never enable it when the AI
  # agents edit the project itself: every file change restarts uvicorn and
  # interrupts the in-flight chat turns (the harness would kill its own work).
  echo "Running DEBUG api with source reload"
  uvicorn codx.junior.main:app --reload --reload-exclude ".venv" --host 0.0.0.0 --port $API_PORT
else
  # DEBUG=1 only raises logging/verbosity here: the API is supervised by
  # supervisor/Docker and must not restart itself while a turn is running.
  echo "Running DEBUG api (no source reload; set CODX_JUNIOR_API_RELOAD=1 to enable)"
  uvicorn codx.junior.main:app --workers ${WEB_CONCURRENCY:-1} --host 0.0.0.0 --port $API_PORT
fi

# One-shot helper: restart the two containers this change needs, a bit after it
# is created, so the turn that schedules it is not killed by its own restart.
#
#   docker compose -f .codx/tmp/restart-stack.compose.yaml up -d
services:
  restart-stack:
    image: docker:cli
    entrypoint: ["sh", "-c", "sleep ${RESTART_DELAY_SECONDS:-90} && docker restart codx-junior-api && docker restart codx-junior-client"]
    volumes:
      - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock

```browser-use/Dockerfile .codx/coworking/images/bu01.browser-use/Dockerfile
# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1
#
# Browser Use — coworking desktop image
#
# Desktop (linuxserver webtop, live view on port 3000) with the browser-use AI
# browser agent ready to drive its own Chromium:
#   https://github.com/browser-use/browser-use
#
# The definition lives in .codx/coworking/images/bu01.browser-use. Credentials
# are never baked into the image: every key below is declared with an empty
# value so the coworking session form (advanced settings -> extra_env) can fill
# it when the session is created.
ARG BASE_IMAGE=lscr.io/linuxserver/webtop:ubuntu-xfce
FROM ${BASE_IMAGE}

# ── Session environment ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Safe defaults are real values; the credential entries are intentionally empty
# and are overwritten by the session (`extra_env`) at runtime.
ENV BROWSER_USE_HOME=/opt/browser-use \
    BROWSER_USE_VENV=/opt/browser-use/.venv \
    BROWSER_USE_HEADLESS=false \
    BROWSER_USE_LOGGING_LEVEL=info \
    BROWSER_USE_CDP_URL=http://127.0.0.1:9222 \
    ANONYMIZED_TELEMETRY=false \
    BROWSER_USE_CLOUD_SYNC=false \
    BROWSER_USE_LLM_MODEL= \
    OPENAI_API_KEY= \
    ANTHROPIC_API_KEY= \
    GOOGLE_API_KEY= \
    DEEPSEEK_API_KEY= \
    OPENROUTER_API_KEY= \
    BROWSER_USE_API_KEY=

# ── System packages ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
USER root
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
RUN apt-get update \
 && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
      build-essential \
      ca-certificates \
      curl \
      git \
      python3 \
      python3-pip \
      python3-venv \
 && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# ── browser-use + its Chromium ────────────────────────────────────────────
# The venv is prepended to PATH further down, so `browser-use` and
# `python -c "import browser_use"` work in every shell of the desktop.
RUN python3 -m venv "${BROWSER_USE_VENV}" \
 && "${BROWSER_USE_VENV}/bin/pip" install --no-cache-dir --upgrade pip wheel \
 && "${BROWSER_USE_VENV}/bin/pip" install --no-cache-dir "browser-use[cli]" playwright

# Chromium plus the system libraries it needs (installed by Playwright itself,
# the same path browser-use recommends upstream).
RUN "${BROWSER_USE_VENV}/bin/python" -m playwright install --with-deps chromium \
 && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

ENV PATH=${BROWSER_USE_VENV}/bin:${PATH}

# ── Support files ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# The menu entry lives in /usr/share/applications so it survives the /config
# volume of the base desktop.
COPY support/check-browser-use.sh /opt/coworking/check-browser-use.sh
COPY support/browser-use.env.example /opt/coworking/browser-use.env.example
COPY support/desktop/browser-use.desktop /usr/share/applications/browser-use.desktop
# The venv is only read+execute for the desktop user (`chmod a+rX` below); the
# recursive `chown -R` used to copy up every file of the venv during the build
# and stalled the build for minutes. Only the top level is handed to `abc`.
RUN chmod +x /opt/coworking/check-browser-use.sh \
 && chmod -R a+rX /opt/browser-use /opt/coworking \
 && chown abc:abc /opt/browser-use

# ── Metadata ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
ARG IMAGE_VERSION=1.0.0
LABEL org.opencontainers.image.title="Browser Use" \
      org.opencontainers.image.version="${IMAGE_VERSION}" \
      org.opencontainers.image.description="Coworking desktop with the browser-use AI browser agent" \
      org.opencontainers.image.source="codx-junior:coworking/browser-use"

USER abc
EXPOSE 3000

```
